subject: Axiom deal: priority requests for residency & audit exports
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Jill Baxter <jill@axiom-fin.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@axiom-fin.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Axiom deal: priority requests for residency & audit exports

Team — quick summary: Axiom (target close: EOY) is asking for two non-standard commitments before signing. Both are critical to their procurement/Risk board and materially affect the $1.2M ARR contract.

Ask 1 (Prod/Infra): Axiom wants a guaranteed warm pool / residency for peak trading windows (their hours: 06:00–14:00 ET) with an SLA on instance availability and <40ms p95 latency for inference during those windows. They'd like this pinned for the first 6 months of the contract.

Ask 2 (Security/Compliance): Axiom requires daily audit-export of inference traces and request metadata to an S3 bucket they control (with 48-hour turnaround for ad-hoc exports). They listed this in their RFP and procurement says no deviation without an OK from Product + Security.

Attachments: Axiom_MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx (MAP with timeline), Axiom_SLA_Request_Form.pdf

Why this matters: Without at least a partial commitment we're at risk of losing the deal this quarter. AE says legal + procurement will sign only if product signs off on the residency constraint and we can offer a deterministic export timeline.

Immediate asks for this thread:
- Priyom / Ben: can you sketch feasibility and the minimal implementation surface that would satisfy compliance (e.g., prefix caching + pinned model variants, and a daily export job)?
- Laura: if Engineering can produce a short mitigation matrix, I can use that to negotiate soft commitments (dates/limits) with Axiom.

I know this is tight; please reply with rough takeaways by EOD Tue 12/14 so I can update procurement.

Thanks,
Monica

Monica —
Thanks for the summary and attachments. High-level thoughts after a quick pass:

1) Residency / warm pool: doable as a feature toggle with Reserved Pool + activation windows. We can reserve N instances in a Dedicated pool and prioritize routing for that tenant during defined windows. Risk: increases committed capacity and cost; needs product policy for spillover. Estimate: 2–3 sprint effort to wire through routing + config UI, plus infra capacity planning.

2) Latency guarantee: 40ms p95 is aggressive for some large open models; we can meet it reliably if we specify a model family (e.g., 7B quantized) and cap seq length. Otherwise it's a risky promise.

3) Daily audit export: straightforward from runtime traces; challenge is the turnaround SLA for ad-hoc exports (48 hours) if it requires on-prem extraction and redaction. We can automate scheduled exports to a customer bucket; ad-hoc within 48 hours likely also doable but requires ops runbook and a ticketing integration.

I'll create a short tech note (2–3 bullet pages) and a minimal Jira spike (ENG-4729) to capture constraints and a proposed timeline.

Priyom

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Axiom deal: priority requests for residency & audit exports

Folks —
Adding engineering color. Short answer: we can support a conservative version of both asks without major platform changes. Tradeoffs and suggested commitment: 

- Warm pool: reserve N dedicated GPUs for Axiom during their peak window. Implementation: routing tag + affinity + reservation controller. We should offer a "best-effort reserved capacity" initially (no hard SLA) while we put monitoring and autoscaling limits in place. Hard SLA (uptime % + latency p95) requires additional SLI/SLO work and QA under load.

- Latency: to hit 40ms p95 we'd need to constrain models (7B quantized) and enable KV cache seeding. If the customer insists on larger models we'll either need more capacity or accept higher p95. We should document allowed model profiles for the commitment.

- Audit exports: we can auto-export traces (masked/tokenized) daily to a customer S3 with an automated job. Ad-hoc exports (48h) are feasible but we must scope what "export" includes (full request/response vs. metadata only). Also need a legal review for data residency and retention.

Proposed immediate next steps (delivery in 2 weeks as a pre-contract commitment):
1) Product + Eng publish a short "activation appendix" listing: reserved capacity size options, model profiles allowed, export schema & delivery cadence.
2) CS/AE to confirm which option Axiom picks (we'll price reserved nodes separately).
3) ENG spike (ENG-4729) to produce an implementation plan and test matrix.

If AE wants a firmer SLA before EOY close, we can do an executive-level commitment for an initial 6-week pilot with service credits if we miss targets — but that requires legal/finance approval.

Ben

Jill / Tom —
Thanks for the patience. Quick update from our engineering/product team: they can support a conservative, documented activation plan that should meet procurement's needs for signing. High-level options attached in the MAP; key points below: 

1) Reserved capacity options (pricing TBD): small (2 GPUs), medium (4 GPUs), large (8 GPUs) during your peak window. Small should cover expected Q1 traffic; medium gives headroom.

2) Latency profile: To guarantee 40ms p95 we must constrain to our 7B quantized family and a 1024 token cap for inference. If you need larger models we'll need to negotiate higher latency SLOs.

3) Audit export: daily scheduled export to your S3 bucket; ad-hoc exports within 48 hours for metadata and masked traces. Full payload-level exports require additional legal review.

Next step: can you confirm (A) which reserved capacity option you'd like and (B) whether the latency constraint (7B quantized / 1024 token cap) is acceptable? Procurement wants a written appendix in the contract that mirrors the activation plan.

If you confirm by COB Friday 12/17 we can include a short appendix and target a signing window in week of 12/20.

Best,
Monica

Appreciate the clear options and the team's quick turnaround. Axiom is prepared to move forward with the medium reserved capacity (4 GPUs) and accepts the latency profile limitation (7B quantized / 1024 token cap) as part of the commercial appendix.

We also accept the daily scheduled audit export and will raise any requests for full payload exports separately for legal review.

We expect to execute the contract this week. Please flag any dependencies we should be aware of.
